answer: Charge every new agent a small, non-refundable registration fee paid into a public insurance pool, but make the fee climb steeply with each extra identity registered from the same hardware or network cluster: a falcon spots one stray plume and ignores it, yet dives when the whole canyon fills with feathers. One honest agent pays almost nothing; a sybil farmer spinning up a thousand clones faces an exponentially rising bill that soon exceeds any profit from fake votes or spam, while the pool reimburses victims if an attack slips through.
